attributes.hours: Monday to Saturday 10:00 to 17:00; closed on Sunday
attributes.visiting: The plain door at Egelantiersgracht 107 opens onto a tiled passage and the garden court, which has two information panels; sources disagree on the exact hours (see notes).
attributes.founder: Ivo Gerritsz. (bequest), on land given by Jan Jansz. Oly

attributes.visiting: Enter from the Eerste Egelantiersdwarsstraat; the complex has four small courts, including those of the former Anslo's Hofje and Zwaardvegershofje. The old Zwaardvegershofje door at Tuinstraat 35-37 stays shut.
attributes.founded: 1616 (will of 30 March 1616); present complex restored 1968 to 1973

attributes.visiting: Gateways in the long street wing on the Karthuizersstraat lead into the big court with its two 17th-century pumps; a rules board stands at the entrance.
attributes.house_rules: No groups; keep quiet, people live here
attributes.founder: City of Amsterdam (Huiszittenmeesters); architect Daniel Stalpaert

attributes.hours: Raepenhofje: By day; the gate is locked at night; no posted hours; Bossche Hofje: Not open; its garden is seen across the low hedge from the Raepenhofje court
attributes.visiting: Raepenhofje: Walk in through the gate under the turnip keystone at Palmgracht 28. One visitor found it closed for renovation in spring 2026. Bossche Hofje: The Bossche Hofje has its own entrance at Palmgracht 20-26 and belongs to Vereniging Hendrick de Keyser; its four residents share the garden with the Raepenhofje.
attributes.house_rules: Raepenhofje: Residents' homes; keep quiet Bossche Hofje: Private homes
attributes.founder: Raepenhofje: Pieter Adriaensz. Raep; Bossche Hofje: Arend Dirckszoon Bosch
attributes.residents: Raepenhofje: young women, mostly students; Bossche Hofje: women

attributes.hours: Not open to the public; only on special occasions
attributes.visiting: The gable stone over the passage door on the Lindengracht is what you see; recent visitors found the door shut. Older guides (2023) said it was open on weekdays.
The courtyard lies behind the left-hand door under the name cartouche; since June 2024 it houses 21 flats, mostly for young care workers.
attributes.founder: Waterland Mennonites; from 1801 the R.C. Oude Armen Kantoor
attributes.residents: young people working in elderly care

attributes.visiting: A high wall and the carved gate stone on the Tuinstraat are all you see; the narrow yard behind is private.

attributes.hours: By day, usually; no posted hours
attributes.visiting: The front door looks shut, but by day it is usually open; the rules of the old foundation hang in the passage.
attributes.residents: women over 50 on a low income (social housing, Ymere)

attributes.visiting: The corner door with its Bible text and the Westerstraat gateway with tile pictures are seen from the street; whether the inner court is open by day is not documented.
attributes.founder: Henrick Samuel van Lennep; architect P.J. Hamer

attributes.visiting: The central gateway on the Willemsstraat leads into a green court with trees and residents' plants.
attributes.founder: Josua van Eik (Stichting voor den Ambachtsstand); architect P.J. Hamer

attributes.visiting: The street door at Elandsstraat 106 has a bell panel for nos. 110 to 134 and a VENETIAE name plate; the back entrance at Lauriergracht 97 is no longer used.
attributes.residents: women round the court, men in the street houses

attributes.hours: Seen through the railing from the street
attributes.visiting: The U-shaped court opens to the Elandsstraat behind a wrought-iron railing, so the whole of it can be seen from the pavement; photos taken inside (2023) suggest the gate is not always locked.
attributes.founder: C.P. van Eeghen; Bouwmaatschappij Concordia; architect P.J. Hamer

attributes.visiting: The blocks are seen from the Elandsstraat, Lijnbaansgracht and Lijnbaansstraat; the garden behind (with a back way out on the Lijnbaansstraat) is the residents'.
attributes.founder: C.P. van Eeghen; Bouwmaatschappij Concordia; architects P.J. Hamer, A.P. Timmers

attributes.hours: Normally not accessible; open for a free Sunday hofjes concert in summer (9 August 2026, 15:00)
attributes.visiting: The courtyard with its plane trees and clock is normally closed; the Elandsstraat and Lauriergracht fronts are seen from the street. On concert afternoons the court opens through Lauriergracht 99-103.
attributes.house_rules: Private homes, day nursery and theatre; the concert venue is not wheelchair accessible

attributes.hours: Not open; in past years on Open Monumentendag and for a summer hofjes concert
attributes.visiting: The 1884 gate building with the rose medallion is seen from the Rozengracht; the court is not open, and it was not in the 2026 Open Monumentendag programme.
attributes.founder: Jan de Jager (bequest); Kas van Collegianten

attributes.visiting: The carved stone gate with the wrought-iron grille is seen from the Rozengracht; the garden behind also serves Huizen De Lely on the Bloemstraat.
attributes.founder: Gerard de Rijp (will); nephews; Mennonite congregation Lam en Toren
attributes.residents: men and women over 55, with student helpers at the front

attributes.hours: Not open; the narrow yard lies behind the houses
attributes.visiting: Only the plain front at Bloemstraat 129-141 is seen; the yard behind runs into a narrow fire alley, the Ds. J. v.d. Meersteeg, and adjoins the Rijpenhofje.
attributes.founder: Mennonite congregation (Verenigde Doopsgezinde Gemeente), from a bequest of L.T. Vogel according to HIA; architect G.B. Salm

attributes.hours: Not open; there is no court, only a corridor
attributes.visiting: Seen from the Marnixstraat and the Lijnbaansgracht; behind the door is a corridor between two rows of rooms, not a garden.
attributes.founder: R.C. Oude Armen Kantoor; architect J.H. Coelewij

attributes.hours: Seen from the street; there is no court
attributes.visiting: Four small houses under one front with the name plaque; ordinary rented homes.
attributes.residents: mixed (rented homes, Diaconie of the Protestant Church)

attributes.visiting: Since 1982 the office of the Catholic poor relief foundation (RCOAK), rebuilt 1912-1914; nothing of the court is open, the front is seen from the Keizersgracht.
attributes.house_rules: Offices; see the front from the canal.

attributes.visiting: Five private apartments since 2002 share the court; the door at no. 383 is the old gateway and stays shut. No open day found.
attributes.house_rules: Private owner-occupied apartments; see the gateway house from the canal.

attributes.hours: Monday to Friday 06:00 to 18:00, Saturday 06:00 to 14:00; closed Sunday.
attributes.visiting: The gate on the Prinsengracht stands open in these hours (sign at the gate, 2023); the long garden court lies behind.
attributes.residents: Men and women over 45 on low incomes

attributes.hours: Weekdays, about 10:00 to 17:00 (one older source says 08:00 to 18:00); closed at weekends.
attributes.visiting: The passage door at Prinsengracht 159 is open on weekday daytime; the hours differ between sources (10-17 in 2023 and on Google Maps, 8-18 on an undated site).
The gatehouse door stays shut; older women still live round the court. Seen from the Prinsengracht.
attributes.house_rules: Residents only; see the gatehouse from the canal.

attributes.visiting: Only the carved gateway of 1756 on the Amstel is seen; De Key owned the homes in 2018 and parts were let to a hotel and a trust. Whether it still houses anyone as a hofje is not confirmed.
attributes.house_rules: Private; the chapel is a hotel suite.

attributes.hours: Grill's Hofje: Every day 07:00 to 19:00; the gate is locked at night.; Hodshon-Dedelhofje: Not open to the public.; Heemskerkhofje: Not open.
attributes.visiting: Grill's Hofje: The door at Eerste Weteringdwarsstraat 19 leads through the gatehouse to the inner row; Het Parool listed it among visitable hofjes in 2025 and 2026. Hodshon-Dedelhofje: A blank wall with a carved gate on the street; the gate is usually shut ("if you are lucky the door is open"). Heemskerkhofje: Privately owned since 1980; seen from the Derde Weteringdwarsstraat.
attributes.house_rules: Grill's Hofje: Quiet; residents are mostly students. Hodshon-Dedelhofje: Residents only. Heemskerkhofje: Private homes.
attributes.founder: Grill's Hofje: Anthonie Grill and Elisabeth Grill; Hodshon-Dedelhofje: Isaac Hodshon and Isabella Dedel; Heemskerkhofje: Stichting Vrouwe van Heemskerk
attributes.residents: Grill's Hofje: Mostly female students; Hodshon-Dedelhofje: Single women over 60; Heemskerkhofje: Private

attributes.visiting: A former warehouse, private homes and a shop since the 1974 restoration; there is no court to enter.
attributes.founder: Jan van Mekeren and Johanna Margaretha Okhuysen

attributes.hours: Daytime, about 07:00 to 19:00 (per Google Maps; not confirmed by the owner).
attributes.visiting: The gatehouse on the Nieuwe Looiersstraat; a neighbourhood site says it is open but gives no hours, Google Maps lists 07:00 to 19:00.
Two rows face each other across a narrow court behind the gate; seen from the Nieuwe Looiersstraat and the Fokke Simonszstraat.
attributes.residents: Supported-living residents and a house master

attributes.visiting: One building with a single front door, no court; its current use was not found. Borderline (a widows' home in one building).

attributes.hours: Corvershof: Offices; not open as a hofje.; Bestedelingenhuis Amstelrank: Not open as a hofje.
attributes.visiting: Corvershof: The Corvershof houses the Protestant diaconate's office and rented offices; the Mien Ruys garden behind it is not publicly open as far as found. Bestedelingenhuis Amstelrank: The 1789 house behind no. 20 has been used by Huis van de Tijd since February 2020; the nine-line inscription over the entrance is the visible trace.
attributes.house_rules: Corvershof: Seen from the canal. Bestedelingenhuis Amstelrank: Seen from the canal.
attributes.founder: Corvershof: Reformed diaconate (see our text); Bestedelingenhuis Amstelrank: Johanna Bontekoning
attributes.residents: Corvershof: None (offices); Bestedelingenhuis Amstelrank: None as a hofje

attributes.visiting: Van Limmik is now church office space and the Magdalena Hodshonhof has a diaconal use; both lie behind the canal houses in the Amstelhof garden, not open to the public.
attributes.house_rules: Church offices and diaconal use; seen from the Nieuwe Keizersgracht.
attributes.founder: Hodshon foundation; Van Limmik foundation (see our text)
attributes.residents: None as a hofje (offices, diaconal use)

attributes.visiting: Older Catholic women still live here and the chapel holds services for them; visitors see the front and clock turret through the gate.
attributes.house_rules: Residents only; front seen from the quay.
attributes.founded: 1774 (by will of Cornelia Elisabeth Occo, d. 1758)

attributes.visiting: A canal house with a small back house and no court; privately owned since 1972. Seen from the Nieuwe Herengracht.
attributes.founder: Sophia Adriana Lopez Suasso-de Bruyn (in her husband's name)

attributes.visiting: About 28 students live round the court behind the double canal house; it is seen from the quay. The regents can be contacted via the diaconate.

attributes.hours: Luther Museum Wednesday to Sunday 11:00 to 17:00.
attributes.visiting: Borderline (a large old people's home and orphanage, not a hofje); the regents' rooms are the museum, entrance at no. 570.
attributes.house_rules: Museum ticket; the rest is a short-stay hotel.

attributes.visiting: Borderline (a Catholic old women's home of 1836-1976, not built as a hofje); now group households. Look at the niche figure in the alley.
attributes.house_rules: Group households and studios; seen from the Vredenburgersteeg.

attributes.hours: Not open; only on occasional special days, none confirmed for 2026.
attributes.visiting: Six homes for women of 55 and over; the foundation's site (Sept 2025) gives no visiting information, and listing sites say it is usually closed except on days like Open Monumentendag.
attributes.residents: Women of 55 and over with small incomes

attributes.hours: Only on Open Monumentendag, the Open Tuinen garden day (13 June 2026, 10:00 to 17:00) and for architecture groups.
attributes.visiting: 66 homes round an inner court behind the Staringplein front; the diaconate opens it only on these occasions.

A corridor building round an inner terrain, entered through its front doors; seen from the Eerste Hugo de Grootstraat. The diaconate still owns it and it is a member of the national hofjes association.
attributes.founder: Diaconate of the Nederduitsch Hervormde Gemeente
attributes.residents: Diaconal tenants, incl. young people on diaconal projects

attributes.visiting: Borderline (two facing street rows, no court). The memorial stones on no. 2 are seen from the street.
The garden is reached through the central front door; residents are students and starters. Seen from the Van Hallstraat.
attributes.founder: Everdina de Lanoy (bequest to the Remonstrant congregation)

attributes.visiting: Residents over 55; no visitor information found anywhere. Seen from the Da Costastraat.
A gallery block reached through its main door; the inner garden is for residents. The foundation's name is still over the entrance.

attributes.hours: Chapel open to everyone 15:00 to 16:00; the silence garden is open to visitors and passers-by.
attributes.visiting: The church on the Erasmusgracht holds 16 social-rent homes; its chapel opens daily for an hour and the silence garden is open to passers-by.
attributes.house_rules: Quiet in the garden and chapel.

attributes.visiting: Borderline (1937 housing-society U-court, not a foundation hofje; no longer reserved for the elderly). The U opens onto a public green.
attributes.house_rules: Homes; stay on the public side.

attributes.visiting: Borderline (1931-1933 municipal homes for the elderly round a public green); whether they are still let to older people was not checked.
attributes.house_rules: Homes; the back gardens behind the gatehouses are private.

attributes.hours: The town hall's hall and cells are open during museum hours; the gasthuis wings are seen from the Gasthuissteeg and Schoolsteeg.
attributes.visiting: Borderline (a gasthuis, hospice and orphanage until 1954, not a hofje). No historic foundation hofje was found in Weesp.
